name: Wayward Haint

source.note: The Crooked Moon (Legends of Avantris), appendix A. Numbers are the book's; the words are ours.

traits.name: Bottle Trap
traits.summary: Entering the space of an upright empty bottle: DC 16 Cha save or it is sucked in and corked.
traits.text: If the haint moves into a space holding an empty bottle standing upright, it makes a DC 16 Charisma saving throw. On a failure it is pulled inside and a stopper seals the bottle. Bottled, it can see and hear 10 feet out and be heard that far. Breaking or opening the bottle lets it out.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.summary: Moves through creatures and objects as Difficult Terrain; 5 (1d10) Force if it ends a turn inside one.
traits.text: The haint passes through creatures and objects as though they were Difficult Terrain, and takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

opening_wail.name: Opening Wail
opening_wail.summary: Its first turn in the fight is a wail: it does nothing else.
opening_wail.text: A haint turned hostile spends its first turn wailing its grief, which warns the party what it has become (ours, R10 decision 28).

actions.name: Draining Regret
actions.summary: +4, 3d6 Psychic and 1 Exhaustion (not past 5; this Exhaustion ends on a rest or Lesser Restoration).
actions.text: Its grief washes over the target: 10 (3d6) Psychic damage and one level of Exhaustion. This can't take the target past 5 levels, and every level it gave goes away when the target finishes a Short or Long Rest or receives Lesser Restoration or similar magic.

summary: A lost soul tied to the regret it can't let go of: it drifts through walls, and its touch leaves the living worn out with sorrow.
